name: Race car front corner, double wishbone, pushrod (synthetic geometry)
source: Synthetic geometry designed for this project (not a real car). Proportions follow common open-wheel and prototype practice: short-long arms, pushrod to a chassis rocker, front-mounted tie rod. Values in mm, kg, N/mm, N.s/mm.

tie_rod.note: inner point placed for minimum bump steer (Nelder-Mead over y, z; residual 2e-4 deg over +/-40 mm)

stops.note: bump stop and droop stop on the spring line, touching at these wheel travels (mm); progressive force k d + k2 d^2 + c dd/dt on the spring-line penetration d, rates N/mm and N/mm^2, damping N.s/mm. A stiff progressive rubber (about 15 mm of compression for an 80 mm stone at 30 km/h). Without them the pushrod rocker goes over center near +90 mm and the linkage locks.

camber_shim.note: shim at the upper ball joint, + spaces the joint outboard on the upright: the wheel top tilts inboard (more negative camber)

caster_shim.note: + moves the upper ball joint forward in the car (eccentric or shims on the upper wishbone; the arms reach the moved joint): the steering axis tilts forward, less caster

arb.note: bar torsion rate in N.m/rad; vertical drop link from a horizontal rocker arm to a horizontal bar arm

tire.note: vertical tire rate N/mm, damping N.s/mm

bushings.note: inboard link bushings for compliance: N/mm and N.m/rad
